chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about a woman who experienced postnatal bleeding, then remained for thirty nights or more, became pure, and performed salat (prayer), then afterward saw blood or yellowish discharge.

So he عليه السلام said: If it is yellowish discharge, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) and perform salat (prayer), and she should not refrain from salat (prayer). But if it is blood that is not yellowish discharge, then let her refrain from salat (prayer) for the days of her menstrual period, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) and perform salat (prayer).

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer whose performance depends on ritual state
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required for purification in this context
key_terms.قُرْئِهَا: the days of her menstrual period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman sees blood or yellowish discharge after becoming pure from nifas?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who becomes pure after nifas and later sees either yellowish discharge or actual blood. It distinguishes between the two, ruling that yellowish discharge does not stop salat (prayer), while actual blood is treated according to the days of her menstrual cycle before she resumes salat (prayer) after ghusl.
